controls.title: Ensure Administrative accounts are cloud-only
controls.description: Privileged roles must be held by cloud-only accounts that are not synchronised from on-premises Active Directory.
controls.rationale: A compromised on-premises directory can be used to pivot into the tenant if privileged identities are synchronised.
controls.auditProcedure:
# Get privileged role IDs
$PrivilegedRoles = $DirectoryRoles | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -like "*Administrator*" -or $_.DisplayName -eq "Global Reader" }
# Get the members of these various roles
$RoleMembers = $PrivilegedRoles | ForEach-Object { Get-MgDirectoryRoleMember -DirectoryRoleId $_.Id } | Select-Object Id -Unique
# Retrieve details about the members in these roles
$PrivilegedUsers = $RoleMembers | ForEach-Object { Get-MgUser -UserId $_.Id -Property UserPrincipalName, DisplayName, Id, OnPremisesSyncEnabled }
$PrivilegedUsers | Where-Object { $_.OnPremisesSyncEnabled -eq $true } | ft DisplayName,UserPrincipalName,OnPremisesSyncEnabled
controls.remediationProcedure: Remediation will require first identifying the privileged accounts that are synced from on-premises and then creating a new cloud-only account for that user. Once a replacement account is established, the hybrid account should have its role reduced to that of a nonprivileged user or removed depending on the need.

audit.name: List synchronised privileged accounts
audit.payload:
$roles = @(Get-MgDirectoryRole) | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -like '*Administrator*' -or $_.DisplayName -eq 'Global Reader' }
$adminUpns = @($roles | ForEach-Object { $_.Members }) | Sort-Object -Unique
$users = @(Get-MgUser)
$synced = @($users | Where-Object { $adminUpns -contains $_.UserPrincipalName -and $_.OnPremisesSyncEnabled -eq $true })
[pscustomobject]@{ PrivilegedAccountCount = $adminUpns.Count; SyncedPrivilegedAccounts = @($synced | ForEach-Object { $_.UserPrincipalName }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 -Compress

assertions.failure: Privileged roles are held by accounts synchronised from on-premises Active Directory: {actual}.
assertions.hint: Create cloud-only replacement accounts for these identities, move the role assignment across, then reduce the hybrid account to a standard user.

controls.title: Ensure that between two and four global admins are designated
controls.description: The Global Administrator role must be held by at least two and no more than four accounts.
controls.rationale: A single global admin is an availability risk; too many multiply the tenant's attack surface.
controls.auditProcedure:
# Determine Id of role using the immutable RoleTemplateId value.
$globalAdminRole = Get-MgDirectoryRole -Filter "RoleTemplateId eq '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10'"
$globalAdmins = Get-MgDirectoryRoleMember -DirectoryRoleId $globalAdminRole.Id
Write-Host "*** There are" $globalAdmins.AdditionalProperties.Count "Global Administrators assigned."

Graph API:
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/security/secureScores
controls.remediationProcedure:
To remediate using the UI:
1. Navigate to the Microsoft 365 admin center https://admin.microsoft.com
2. Select Users > Active Users.
3. In the Search field enter the name of the user to be made a Global Administrator.
4. To create a new Global Admin: select the user's name, select Manage roles, select Admin center access, check Global Administrator, click Save changes.
5. To remove Global Admins: select the user, under Roles select Manage roles, de-select the appropriate role, click Save changes.

assertions.failure: The tenant has {actual} Global Administrators; CIS requires between {expected} and {secondary}.
assertions.hint: Assign or remove Global Administrator role holders until between two and four accounts remain, keeping one dedicated break-glass account.

controls.title: Ensure sign-in to shared mailboxes is blocked
controls.description: The Entra ID account backing every shared mailbox must be disabled so it cannot be used to sign in interactively.
controls.rationale: Shared mailbox accounts have a known password-less identity; leaving sign-in enabled gives an attacker a foothold that no one monitors.
controls.nistCategory: PR.AA-01 Identities and credentials are managed
controls.auditProcedure:
$MBX = Get-EXOMailbox -RecipientTypeDetails SharedMailbox
$MBX | ForEach-Object { Get-MgUser -UserId $_.ExternalDirectoryObjectId -Property DisplayName, UserPrincipalName, AccountEnabled } | Format-Table DisplayName, UserPrincipalName, AccountEnabled
controls.remediationProcedure:
To disable sign-in for a single account:
$MBX = Get-EXOMailbox -Identity TestUser@example.com
Update-MgUser -UserId $MBX.ExternalDirectoryObjectId -AccountEnabled:$false

The following will block sign-in to all Shared Mailboxes:
$MBX = Get-EXOMailbox -RecipientTypeDetails SharedMailbox
$MBX | ForEach-Object { Update-MgUser -UserId $_.ExternalDirectoryObjectId -AccountEnabled:$false }

audit.name: Find shared mailboxes that can still sign in
audit.payload:
$shared = @(Get-EXOMailbox | Where-Object { $_.RecipientTypeDetails -eq 'SharedMailbox' })
$users = @(Get-MgUser)
$enabled = @($shared | Where-Object { $upn = $_.UserPrincipalName; ($users | Where-Object { $_.UserPrincipalName -eq $upn -and $_.AccountEnabled -eq $true }) })
[pscustomobject]@{ SharedMailboxCount = $shared.Count; SignInEnabledMailboxes = @($enabled | ForEach-Object { $_.UserPrincipalName }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 -Compress

assertions.failure: Interactive sign-in is still enabled on these shared mailboxes: {actual}.
assertions.hint: Disable the Entra ID account behind each shared mailbox with Update-MgUser -AccountEnabled:$false.

remediation.name: Block sign-in on every shared mailbox

controls.title: Ensure the 'Password expiration policy' is set to 'Set passwords to never expire'
controls.description: Password expiry must be disabled so users are not driven towards predictable password rotation patterns.
controls.rationale: Forced rotation encourages weak, incremental passwords. NIST and Microsoft both recommend expiry be disabled in favour of MFA and banned-password lists.
controls.nistCategory: PR.AA-01 Identities and credentials are managed

audit.name: Read the domain password validity period

assertions.failure: Passwords expire after {actual} days on this domain; CIS requires the never-expire value {expected}.
assertions.hint: Run Update-MgDomain -PasswordValidityPeriodInDays 2147483647 for every verified domain.

remediation.name: Set passwords to never expire
remediation.payload:
Set-MgDomain -PasswordValidityPeriodInDays 2147483647
Get-MgDomain | Select-Object Id, PasswordValidityPeriodInDays | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

rollback.name: Restore the previous password validity period
rollback.payload:
Set-MgDomain -PasswordValidityPeriodInDays {{PasswordValidityPeriodInDays}}
Get-MgDomain | Select-Object Id, PasswordValidityPeriodInDays | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure 'External sharing' of calendars is not available
controls.description: Anonymous calendar sharing outside the organisation must be turned off.
controls.rationale: Published calendars leak meeting subjects, attendee lists and travel patterns that are useful for social engineering.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Users will no longer be able to publish calendars to external recipients.
controls.auditProcedure: Get-SharingPolicy -Identity "Default Sharing Policy" | Select-Object Domains, Enabled

audit.name: Read the default calendar sharing policy

assertions.failure: The default calendar sharing policy is enabled ({actual}), so users can publish calendars externally.
assertions.hint: Disable the default sharing policy with Set-SharingPolicy -Enabled $false.

remediation.name: Disable external calendar sharing
remediation.payload:
Set-SharingPolicy -Identity 'Default Sharing Policy' -Enabled $false
Get-SharingPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enabled | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

rollback.name: Restore the previous calendar sharing setting
rollback.payload:
Set-SharingPolicy -Identity 'Default Sharing Policy' -Enabled {{Enabled}}
Get-SharingPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enabled | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure the customer lockbox feature is enabled
controls.description: Customer Lockbox requires explicit customer approval before a Microsoft engineer can access tenant content.
controls.rationale: Without Lockbox, support access to customer data happens without an approval record.
controls.remediationProcedure: Set-OrganizationConfig -CustomerLockBoxEnabled $true. Requires Microsoft 365 E5 or the Compliance add-on.

assertions.failure: Customer Lockbox is {actual}; Microsoft support can access tenant content without a recorded customer approval.
assertions.hint: Enable Customer Lockbox once the tenant holds Microsoft 365 E5 or the Compliance add-on.
